questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell drivers about traffic laws in that area. This sign means you cannot turn right.

questions.question: When changing lanes:

options.text: Your mirrors can adequately show you your surroundings.
Do a head check in addition to using your mirrors.
Activate your turn signal and immediately move to the right or left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do a head check in addition to using your mirrors.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots just like other vehicles. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Do not rely only on mirrors.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: Which brake is more powerful on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: Before starting a turn, a motorcyclist should change gears to:

options.text: Prevent a change in power in the middle of the turn.
Be able to keep both hands on the handle grips during the turn.
Prevent the motorcycle from slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent a change in power in the middle of the turn.
questions.explanation: Change gears before you turn. Shifting gears while turning can suddenly change power to the rear wheel and cause a skid. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly to avoid skidding.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle:

options.text: The mirrors provide a perfect view.
The mirrors do not show your blind spots.
The mirrors should not be used, except when parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: The mirrors do not show your blind spots.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle mirrors have blind spots like any other vehicle. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: There may be less traction available for braking when:

options.text: A motorcycle is straight up and down.
A motorcycle is on dry pavement.

questions.explanation: When a motorcycle is leaning, such as in a turn, there is less grip available for braking. You can use both brakes while turning, but you must be very careful.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that traffic is merging ahead.

questions.question: When riding at night, maintain a minimum following distance of:
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge distance in the dark. When riding at night, stay at least three seconds behind the vehicle in front of you.

questions.question: Stopping in a turn can be difficult because:

options.text: There is decreased traction available for stopping while the bike is leaning.
The rider is usually focused on the turn and not on the braking.
The brake controls do not work in turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is decreased traction available for stopping while the bike is leaning.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but be very careful. When the motorcycle is leaning, some grip is used for turning. This leaves less grip for braking.

questions.question: A motorcycle horn is ________ a car horn.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle horn is not as loud as a car horn. Riders should use their horns when needed but should not rely on them for safety.

questions.question: When buying a motorcycle helmet, what should matter most?
questions.explanation: Protection is the most important thing to consider when buying a motorcycle helmet.

questions.question: In normal conditions, what is the minimum distance a motorcyclist should keep between their bike and the vehicle ahead?
questions.explanation: In normal conditions, keep at least two seconds between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead. In bad conditions, keep an even larger distance.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, a motorcyclist should not:

options.text: Position themselves where other drivers can see them.
Have their hands ready on the clutch and brakes.

questions.explanation: When approaching an intersection, choose a lane position that makes you visible to other drivers. Have your hands ready on the clutch and brakes. Slow down as you approach. Do not suddenly change speed or position, as this confuses other drivers.

questions.question: Which of these is not a hazard?

options.text: Road conditions that stay the same as you ride

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions that stay the same as you ride
questions.explanation: Look ahead and plan to manage hazards you may see. This includes changes in the road and surrounding traffic.

questions.question: You should flash your brake light to:

options.text: Show other drivers you are nearby.
Help other drivers see you in slow traffic.
Warn other drivers that you are slowing down or stopping unexpectedly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warn other drivers that you are slowing down or stopping unexpectedly.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light to alert other drivers when you slow down or stop where they may not expect it. This is especially important before making tight turns off high-speed roads.

questions.question: Which of these is a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: Surfaces like wet pavement, snow, ice, mud, gravel roads, lane markings, steel plates, and utility covers all have poor traction.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while stopping, you should:

options.text: Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release the front brake right away, then press it firmly again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away, then press it firmly again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks during a quick stop, release the front brake immediately and then press it firmly again. Use both front and rear brakes when you need to stop quickly.

questions.question: If you see a hazard on the road, do not:

options.text: Alert other drivers to your presence.
Use your horn, lights, or signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alert other drivers to your presence.
questions.explanation: Alert other drivers using your horn, lights, and signals. Adjust your speed and position as needed to avoid hazards.

questions.question: When the lights on a railroad crossing sign are flashing, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Turn around and find another route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing lights at a railroad crossing, come to a complete stop. Wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing before moving. Never try to race a train across the tracks.

questions.question: Where should you carry a load on your motorcycle?

options.text: On the gas tank in front of you.
Piled up against the sissy bar or frame on the back of the seat.

questions.explanation: Keep loads over or in front of the rear axle. Only experienced riders should carry loads on a motorcycle.

questions.question: When turning, what should you do?

options.text: Move your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head, not your shoulders, to look through the turn.
Turn your head and shoulders to look through the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head, not your shoulders, to look through the turn.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn to where you want to go. Turn only your head, keeping your eyes level with the horizon. Do not turn your shoulders, as this may cause you to steer off course.

questions.question: Riding on ______ may provide poor traction.
questions.explanation: Poor traction can happen on wet, snowy, icy, or muddy pavement, gravel, lane markings, steel plates, and utility hole covers.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Increase your ability to be seen.
Invite other road users into your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other road users into your lane.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you be seen and see others. It helps you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and hazards. Your position should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if needed.

questions.question: What should you do to be seen more easily by other drivers?
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors when riding. This makes it easier for other drivers to see you at any time of day.
